reference: No matching GNU or POSIX termpixel command exists. Cases use Bash's documented type/help metadata behavior and the documented termpixel CLI contract. The 2x2 render expectation is an independent hand-rasterization of frame 0 followed by a separate ANSI encoder using the documented RGB upper-half-block format; it was not sampled from bash-os. Bash loadable usage errors use EX_USAGE, which appears as shell status 2.
coverage: Bash loadable type and help synopsis metadata
Version and selftest completion contracts; internal selftest assertions are not independent graphics-operation evidence.
Exact small-frame ANSI output and one bounded demo frame
Zero-frame demo and stdin EOF key-read behavior
Invalid canvas dimensions and unknown option errors
Truecolor environment recognition and bounded ASCII pipe-key decoding.
Equal-color pixel pair emits one background-colored space, verified independently on a 1x2 frame.
exclusions: Raw terminal mode, cursor hiding/restoration, key decoding, escape timing and interactive animation need a private PTY driver, which the fixture runner does not provide; see deferred case termpixel-pty-input.
No GNU/POSIX implementation of termpixel exists, so operation cases are contract checks rather than GNU parity comparisons.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t should identify the registered loadable as a builtin.
Bash help -s should expose the builtin synopsis declared in the public loadable metadata.
The documented --version option prints the fixed termpixel version.
The documented selftest subcommand succeeds and prints its completion line.
With redirected stdout, /dev/null stdin, and no COLORTERM, probe reports no terminal dimensions, no tty input, and unknown truecolor support.
A tiny frame checks the truecolor upper-half-block renderer, row reset, clipping and two foreground/background color changes against an independently calculated byte stream.
One explicitly bounded animation frame should add the documented home-position sequence and render the same frame-0 pixels as render-demo.
A zero-frame demo is a bounded no-op: it accepts valid dimensions, emits no terminal bytes, and exits successfully.
With no controlling terminal and runner-provided /dev/null stdin, a zero-timeout key read reports EOF as documented.
The canvas contract requires even pixel height; an odd height is rejected as a usage error.
An unrecognized render option is rejected as a usage error rather than producing a frame.
Exercise raw-mode setup/restoration, cursor hygiene, and ASCII/CSI arrow decoding using an isolated pseudo-terminal.
cases.reason: Only headless pipe decoding executes. Raw-mode entry/restoration, cursor controls and escape decoding on a PTY need only the existing PTY driver.

cases.purpose: Probe recognizes both documented truecolor environment spellings in a non-PTY fixture.
cases.script:
COLORTERM=truecolor termpixel probe
COLORTERM=24bit termpixel probe
cases.stdout:
cols=-1 rows=-1 truecolor=yes tty=no
cols=-1 rows=-1 truecolor=yes tty=no

cases.purpose: Decode one ordinary ASCII key from pipe stdin in the headless fixture.
A one-column two-pixel frame has both pixels on the green diagonal. The documented equal-color encoding is a green background plus one space, followed by row reset and newline.
